observations.text: SP performed the overshoot at the level desired for this Training Section, informing the formation leader and displacing behind No1's 6 o'clock only after the IP directed the initial correction. Distance behind No1 was then held near the 80-foot value and the A/C was kept lower than the leading A/C throughout the pass. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent recognition of the excessive overtake before the IP's direction is expected to improve.

SP, having recognized the excessive overtake during the rejoin, informed the formation leader and initiated the overshoot after the IP's verbal cue, crossing No1's 6 o'clock lower and with more than two ship lengths of spacing. Distance behind No1 was kept at the 200-foot value and the reposition to rejoin from inside the leader's turn was completed with a short delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP identified the excessive angle-off during the rejoin, informed the formation leader without delay and executed the overshoot on own initiative. SP passed behind and lower than No1's 6 o'clock with distance behind No1 of about 140 feet, between the 80-foot and 200-foot values, and corrected the deviation in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP assessed the closure and the angle-off early, informed the formation leader and executed the overshoot on own initiative, passing safely behind and lower than No1's 6 o'clock. Distance behind No1 and altitude separation from No1 were held within the 80-foot values, and the reposition to rejoin was flown from inside the leader's turn without abrupt maneuvers. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP anticipated the excessive overtake before it developed, informed the formation leader and executed the overshoot with precise power and energy management. Deviations in distance behind No1 and in altitude separation from No1 were negligible against the 80-foot values, the crossing of No1's 6 o'clock was flown well clear of two ship lengths and the rejoin from inside the leader's turn required no correction. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a delayed power reduction after recognizing the excessive overtake, did not pass safely behind and lower than No1's 6 o'clock and allowed the A/C to rise toward the leading A/C's level. Altitude separation from No1 departed beyond the 200-foot value and the crossing was made without the minimum spacing of two ship lengths, with the result that the IP directed the correction and executed part of the repositioning. Overshoot geometry and power control require further work.

SP, due to a perceptual error in judging closure and lateral separation, did not inform the formation leader in a timely manner and continued the rejoin instead of initiating the overshoot. Distance behind No1 exceeded the 200-foot value before any displacement was made and the reposition to rejoin from inside the leader's turn was not attempted, with the result that the IP took the A/C and re-established the formation geometry.

SP executed the overshoot at the level desired for this Training Section, informing the formation leader and displacing behind No1's 6 o'clock after the IP's verbal prompt. Distance behind No1 settled at the 200-foot value and the deviation was recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier recognition of the excessive overtake without IP prompting is expected to improve.

SP recognized the excessive angle-off on own initiative, informed the formation leader and executed the overshoot without prompting, passing behind and lower than No1's 6 o'clock. Distance behind No1 opened to about 130 feet, between the 80-foot and 200-foot values, and was corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP assessed the excessive overtake early and informed the formation leader, executing the overshoot with accurate power and bank control. SP crossed No1's 6 o'clock lower and with more than two ship lengths of spacing, held distance behind No1 and altitude separation from No1 within the 80-foot values and repositioned to rejoin from inside the leader's turn without abrupt maneuvers. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP anticipated the developing overtake, informed the formation leader early and executed the overshoot with precise control of energy and geometry. Distance behind No1 and altitude separation from No1 showed negligible deviation from the 80-foot values, the pass behind and below No1's 6 o'clock was flown well outside two ship lengths and the subsequent rejoin from inside the leader's turn required no correction. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a bank input applied toward the leading A/C during the displacement, did not pass safely behind and lower than No1's 6 o'clock. The crossing was made without the minimum spacing of two ship lengths and altitude separation from No1 departed beyond the 200-foot value, with the result that the IP intervened on the controls to re-establish separation.

SP, due to continuation of the plan after the information that invalidated it had already been received, pressed the rejoin with excessive overtake instead of calling and executing the overshoot. Distance behind No1 exceeded the 200-foot value before any displacement was made and the formation leader was informed only after the IP's direction, with the result that the IP directed the break out and flew part of the repositioning. A timely decision to overshoot is required.

SP, due to a late and insufficient power reduction, did not cross No1's 6 o'clock with the minimum spacing of two ship lengths and did not reposition to rejoin from inside the leader's turn in a timely manner. Distance behind No1 reached the 200-foot value and the deviation was recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal directions.

SP, due to failure to shed a secondary task when workload increased, informed the formation leader late and delayed the overshoot decision during the turning rejoin. Altitude separation from No1 reached the 200-foot value and the A/C drifted toward the leader's 3/9 o'clock line, with the result that the correction was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts.

SP executed the overshoot within the desired standards, informing the formation leader and passing behind and lower than No1's 6 o'clock without IP's intervention. Distance behind No1 twice opened to about 150 feet, between the 80-foot and 200-foot values, before being corrected. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency in spacing control during the pass behind No1 is expected to improve.

SP recognized the excessive overtake early, informed the formation leader immediately and executed the overshoot with accurate control of power and bank. Distance behind No1 was held within the 80-foot value, altitude separation from No1 within the 80-foot value, and the A/C was kept behind the leader's 3/9 o'clock line throughout the pass. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP anticipated the excessive angle-off before the closure developed, informed the formation leader without delay and flew the overshoot with exceptional accuracy. Deviations in distance behind No1 and in altitude separation from No1 were negligible against the 80-foot values, and the reposition to rejoin from inside the leader's turn was completed smoothly and without any effect on the leader's flight path. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an over-controlled roll input during the displacement behind No1, did not keep the A/C safely behind and lower than No1's 6 o'clock. Altitude separation from No1 departed beyond the 200-foot value toward the leading A/C's level and the crossing was made inside two ship lengths, with the result that the IP took the A/C to re-establish separation. Control harmony during the overshoot requires further work.

SP, due to lack of assertiveness in voicing a recognized unsafe condition, did not inform the formation leader that the rejoin could no longer be saved and continued closing with excessive overtake. Distance behind No1 exceeded the 200-foot value after a late and abrupt displacement and the subsequent rejoin was flown with abrupt maneuvers, with the result that the IP directed and executed part of the overshoot.

SP, due to an insufficient power reduction at the start of the overshoot, did not cross No1's 6 o'clock with the minimum spacing of two ship lengths and did not reposition to rejoin from inside the leader's turn in a timely manner. Distance behind No1 reached the 200-foot value and was corrected with delay, only after the IP's verbal directions.

SP, due to degraded situational awareness after the unplanned change of the rejoin sequence, informed the formation leader late and started the overshoot with the closure already excessive. Altitude separation from No1 reached the 200-foot value during the pass and the A/C drifted toward the leader's 3/9 o'clock line, with the result that the recovery to formation position was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts.

SP, due to a late bank reversal after crossing No1's 6 o'clock, did not reposition to rejoin from inside the leader's turn as promptly as required. Distance behind No1 opened to about 150 feet, between the 80-foot and 200-foot values, with the result of a minor deviation that was recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic during the rejoin, informed the formation leader with slight delay and initiated the overshoot later than the geometry required. Altitude separation from No1 momentarily reached about 140 feet, between the 80-foot and 200-foot values, and SP corrected it in a timely manner without IP's intervention, completing the rejoin without abrupt maneuvers.

SP executed the overshoot with accuracy and speed, informing the formation leader in time and passing safely behind and lower than No1's 6 o'clock. Distance behind No1 and altitude separation from No1 were held within the 80-foot values, however the spacing at the crossing was kept just above the minimum of two ship lengths on both passes. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a larger margin at the crossing of No1's 6 o'clock is expected to improve.

SP anticipated the excessive overtake, informed the formation leader early and executed the overshoot with exceptional accuracy in power, bank and geometry control. Distance behind No1 and altitude separation from No1 showed negligible deviation from the 80-foot values, the pass behind and below No1's 6 o'clock was flown well clear of two ship lengths and the rejoin from inside the leader's turn was completed without any abrupt maneuver. Above end of block MIF achieved.
